claims.claim_text: Indexed Lou Bernard Voigt is high-confidence identified as the landscape architect and wartime OSS designer documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official National Register biography gives the exact distinctive name and explicitly states that he began OSS design work in Washington in 1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from an exact distinctive full name and an authoritative official biography that directly links the person to OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The biography supplies a dated employment sequence from Black Mountain College to SOM and then OSS.
claims.match_notes: The match is not upgraded to confirmed because the indexed personnel file has not been reviewed.

claims.claim_text: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill is the best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation for Lou Bernard Voigt.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official biography places Voigt's SOM site-planning work for Oak Ridge after his September 1943 college tenure and before he began OSS design work in Washington in 1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the exact distinctive name and direct OSS link.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded sequence with no known intervening affiliation; exact transfer date is not supplied.
claims.match_notes: The firm is named as an employer; Oak Ridge is the documented worksite, not a separate employer.

claims.claim_text: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill is also the best-supported last civilian employer before Lou Bernard Voigt's OSS service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official chronology moves from SOM's wartime Oak Ridge site-planning engagement to OSS design employment begun in Washington in 1944.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the exact distinctive name and direct OSS link.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded; the same civilian job legitimately satisfies both categories, which remain separately modeled.
claims.match_notes: Immediate affiliation and last civilian employer are stored as distinct claims even though the same documented job answers both questions.

claims.claim_text: Lou Bernard Voigt taught botany and landscape architecture at Black Mountain College from September 1942 to September 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The National Register biography gives the date range and teaching fields; a contemporary 1943 college announcement lists Voigt on the faculty in botany and landscape architecture and notes service since 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence identity from the exact distinctive name and consistent education and professional chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly dated before the later SOM and OSS roles; not labeled immediate.
claims.match_notes: Earlier documented employment, kept separate from the immediate SOM role.
